chunks: (3) Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Iesa, from Yunus, from Sulayman ibn Salih, who raised it to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said: He said:

Indeed, this talk of yours disgusts the hearts of men, so cast it to them forcefully. Whoever accepts it, add to him; and whoever denies it, leave him. There must be a sedition in which every companion and close friend falls, until even those who split a hair into two (due to strictness) fall in it, until no one remains except us and our Shia.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the reaction of people to the Shia's talk and the coming tribulation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) introduces the principle of *al-taqiyya* (dissimulation) by advising followers to present teachings forcefully, as the initial reaction may be disgust, yet those who accept are to be increased in status. This narration highlights the eschatological reality of the Great Tribulation (*al-Fitnah al-Kubra*), where superficial loyalty dissolves, leaving only the steadfast core of the Shia as the true bearers of the faith.
